:::{#exr-bernoulli-score-sum}
#### Score function of a binary sample

In the setting of @exr-bernoulli-score-contribution,
let $\outbar \eqdef \avgin \outvar_\iobs$ be the [sample mean](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample-mean) of the observed outcomes,
and let $\smeandev \eqdef \avgin \devn_\iobs$ be the sample mean of the [deviations](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-deviation-pop-mean) $\devn_\iobs$.
Assemble the [score function](#def-score) $\score(\prob)$ of the whole [sample](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample)
from the [score](#def-score) contributions,
and show that $\smeandev = \outbar - \prob$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-bernoulli-score-sum}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\score(\prob)
&= \sumin \score_\iobs(\prob)
&& \text{(score of an independent sample is the sum of the score contributions)}\\
&= \sumin \precision \devn_\iobs
&& \text{(score contribution of a binary outcome)}\\
&= \precision \sumin \devn_\iobs
&& \text{($\precision$ is the same for every $\iobs$)}\\
&= \precision \cdot n \smeandev
&& \text{($\textstyle\sumin \devn_\iobs = n \smeandev$, from the definition of $\smeandev$)}\\
&= n \precision \smeandev
&& \text{(reorder the factors)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Now write $\smeandev$ in terms of $\outbar$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\smeandev
&= \avgin \devn_\iobs
&& \text{(definition of $\smeandev$)}\\
&= \avgin (\outvar_\iobs - \prob)
&& \text{(definition of $\devn_\iobs$)}\\
&= \frac{1}{n} \paren{\sumin \outvar_\iobs - \sumin \prob}
&& \text{(split the sum)}\\
&= \frac{1}{n} \paren{\sumof{\vy} - \sumin \prob}
&& \text{(definition of $\sumof{\vy}$)}\\
&= \frac{1}{n} \paren{n \outbar - n \prob}
&& \text{($\sumof{\vy} = n \outbar$ and $\textstyle\sumin \prob = n \prob$)}\\
&= \frac{1}{n} \cdot n (\outbar - \prob)
&& \text{(factor out $n$)}\\
&= \outbar - \prob
&& \text{($\frac{1}{n} \cdot n = 1$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
